topic: Advanced Use of Standard I/O Stream Objects in C++
explanation: In advanced C programming techniques, especially when interfacing with C++-style I/O streams, understanding the underlying implementation and customization of standard I/O objects (such as cin, cout, cerr, and clog) is crucial. These objects are instances of classes derived from stream classes, and their behavior can be customized or extended through advanced techniques like stream manipulators, custom stream buffers, and operator overloading. Mastery of these concepts allows for sophisticated control over input/output operations, enabling optimized, context-aware, or platform-specific I/O handling beyond basic usage.

example_explanation: This example demonstrates advanced manipulation of the standard output stream by creating a custom stream buffer that prepends a timestamp to each output. It showcases how stream buffers can be extended and assigned to standard stream objects like cout, enabling sophisticated, context-aware I/O handling. This technique exemplifies deep control over C++ stream internals, a key aspect of advanced C programming for high-performance or specialized I/O operations.
